metadata.title: Travel and Expense Management Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: Explore how travel and expense management would need to change after an acquisition, mandatory signed e-receipts, autonomous travel agents, or a real-time tax audit that combines those changes.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: An employee belongs to one company policy, books a trip through supported channels, pays with a corporate card or personal funds, submits a receipt and expense report, receives manager approval, and posts the approved amount into one finance system. Human users are assumed to initiate and explain each transaction.
metadata.residualArchitecture: Instead of binding an employee, company, policy, booking actor, payment instrument, receipt, approval, accounting code, and ERP posting into one fixed workflow, the adapted design versions each relationship and its evidence. Acquired entities can retain local rules while sharing controls, supplier-signed evidence can replace paper images, software agents act only through delegated authority, and every booked or spent amount remains traceable to the entity, policy, purpose, evidence, approval, and accounting treatment in effect.
metadata.note: The tests start with organizational change, tax evidence, a new booking actor, and external audit. They are distinct from a failed card feed or unavailable ERP integration.

source.title: Residues: Time, Change, and Uncertainty in Software Architecture
source.author: Barry M. O'Reilly

stressors.name: An acquired business keeps its own ERP, policy, currency, and financial calendar
stressors.detection: Acquisition due diligence, entity and ERP inventories, policy comparison, chart-of-accounts mapping, card programs, tax registrations, close calendars, and employee migration plans.
stressors.attractor: Employees, trips, cards, suppliers, approvals, and expenses belong to a company whose legal and accounting meaning differs from the parent. Forcing one policy or ERP immediately blocks operations, while treating the acquired business as an ungoverned exception prevents consolidated control and reporting.
stressors.businessReaction: Preserve the acquired entity's valid process, establish shared minimum controls, map local policies and accounts explicitly, show unresolved differences, consolidate only comparable measures, and migrate systems and cards in controlled stages.
stressors.residue: Separate person, employment, legal entity, policy set, cost center, card program, currency, tax registration, accounting definition, close calendar, and ERP connector. Every transaction and approval resolves these from the relationship and effective date; governed mappings create a group view without overwriting the local financial meaning.

impacts.effect: Finance control expands from one company workflow to a governed multi-entity spend model.
Controllers get one trusted view while retaining the legal and accounting meaning of each entity's records.
Standardization becomes an explicit mapping with coverage and exceptions rather than replacement of local codes.
Close-cycle reporting is segmented by entity and calendar before producing a comparable group result.
Adds entity mappings, local-to-group reconciliation, close-calendar state, and migration coverage.
Supports local closes and controlled consolidation without pretending that every entity posts identically.
Links one person to effective employment, entity, role, approver, and access relationships.
Versions entity-specific account mappings, posting rules, connector state, and reconciliation evidence.
Connects several ERP and card ecosystems through stable transaction and evidence contracts.
Owns shared financial semantics and staged entity integration with local finance teams.
Makes multi-entity integration depth and gradual finance migration a direct enterprise benchmark.

stressors.name: A tax authority accepts only supplier-signed electronic receipt and invoice evidence
stressors.detection: Final tax rule, e-invoice network specifications, supplier readiness, rejected claims, audit guidance, signature verification, and mandated reporting dates.
stressors.attractor: A clear receipt image and employee declaration are no longer sufficient evidence for deduction or reimbursement. Supplier identity, tax registration, signed line data, correction status, and network acknowledgement become authoritative, while paper and OCR remain useful only as supporting context.
stressors.businessReaction: Capture signed supplier evidence as close to purchase as possible, verify origin and integrity, match it to card, trip, employee, and business purpose, request corrections through the appropriate network, and preserve the complete tax and audit trail.
stressors.residue: Represent evidence as typed, versioned records with issuer, recipient entity, signature, schema, line items, tax meaning, currency, transaction link, correction chain, verification, and retention policy. Images, OCR, card data, and employee statements can support the case but do not overwrite authoritative supplier evidence.

impacts.effect: Audit-ready employee spend depends on verifiable supplier evidence, not manual assembly at month end.
Finance can control and post spend from authoritative evidence with only true exceptions requiring review.
Capture includes network delivery, signature verification, matching, correction state, and missing-evidence follow-up.
Record completeness distinguishes authoritative signed evidence from supporting scans and declarations.
Shows received supplier evidence and asks the employee only for unmatched purpose or exception information.
Starts the expense from verified transaction evidence instead of requiring a paper-first report.
Accepts signed structured evidence alongside images and exposes which source is authoritative.
Preserves signatures, verification, correction chain, access, retention, and audit export.
Derives tax treatment from the verified supplier and line evidence under the entity's current rule set.
Owns the evidence experience with tax, finance platform, supplier-network, and integration teams.
Makes end-to-end electronic evidence and low-touch employee capture a product comparison.

stressors.name: Autonomous travel agents begin booking trips within delegated company budgets
stressors.detection: Corporate travel pilots, non-human booking credentials, repeated machine-generated itineraries, approval questions, traveler disputes, and requests for structured policy and budget APIs.
stressors.attractor: The actor selecting and booking travel is neither the traveler nor a travel manager. Authority depends on purpose, traveler, budget, policy, supplier, time, approval, and revocation, while the human still needs to understand and change the commitment.
stressors.businessReaction: Accept bookings only from verifiably delegated agents, evaluate the same policy and budget controls used for people, request approval when required, preserve traveler choice and intervention, and record an explanation of every search, recommendation, and purchase.
stressors.residue: Introduce a signed delegated-travel intent independent of user session and payment method. It identifies principal, traveler, agent, trip purpose, constraints, policy, budget, approval, allowed suppliers, expiry, evidence, and revocation; search, booking, card, duty-of-care, and expense records bind to the resulting authority decision.

impacts.effect: Travel managers can keep spend controlled before commitment even when software selects and books the trip.
The program applies policy, budget, approval, and supplier controls to delegated-machine booking.
Approval shows the agent's authority, traveler intent, alternatives considered, policy result, and budget effect.
In-policy booking includes valid delegated authority and explainable machine-selected commitments.
Adds agent delegation, structured policy and offer contracts, approval evidence, intervention, and revocation.
Applies one travel-intent and control model across human and autonomous booking channels.
Accepts bounded machine intent and returns explainable policy-compliant options through a stable contract.
Evaluates purpose, traveler, route, supplier, timing, and exception policy independently from the booking actor.
Routes only the judgment needed and records the machine proposal, human decision, and resulting scope.
Owns the supported agent-booking contract with identity, policy, card, and duty-of-care teams.
Raises governed autonomous booking and traveler intervention as a managed-travel benchmark.

stressors.name: A tax authority requests a real-time audit of agent-booked travel in the acquired business
stressors.detection: Formal audit notice, entity and period scope, agent-booked transaction inventory, supplier evidence status, policy decisions, approvals, card matches, and ERP posting reconciliation.
stressors.attractor: Finance must prove that a non-human actor had authority to make each commitment, that the acquired entity's local policy and accounts were applied, and that every deductible amount has valid supplier-signed evidence. A report assembled from final totals cannot reconstruct those decisions reliably.
stressors.businessReaction: Freeze the audit population, provide transaction-level authority, entity, policy, evidence, approval, payment, tax, and posting history, explain exceptions, correct governed records without erasing originals, and reconcile the audit result to both local and group books.
stressors.residue: No new structural change is required: the multi-entity model identifies the legal and accounting context, signed evidence proves supplier and tax facts, and delegated-travel records prove machine authority and human approval. Their shared transaction links produce a reproducible audit trail and reconciliation.

impacts.effect: One trusted control view includes the authority and evidence behind machine-booked spend across entities.
Finance and auditors can reproduce why each transaction was allowed, taxed, approved, and posted.
Every exception connects to the entity rule, agent authority, supplier evidence, decision, and correction path.
Audit-ready completeness includes entity context, delegated authority, signed evidence, and reconciled posting.
Produces the audit population, evidence chain, exceptions, corrections, and local-to-group reconciliation from existing records.
Reuses existing entity, evidence, and authority records instead of pausing close for manual reconstruction.
Exports the signed evidence, decision history, access, and correction chain for the scoped transactions.
Proves the principal, agent, traveler, employee, approver, and entity relationships in effect.
Reconciles each transaction and correction to local posting and the governed group mapping.
Can answer the audit through existing contracts rather than a bespoke forensic data project.
Makes real-time, machine-action-aware auditability a concrete enterprise suite benchmark.
